entries.name: mapie.calibration.VennAbers

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.add_jitter
entries.summary: Add a tiny normal distributed perturbation to an array x.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.cumulative_differences
entries.summary: Compute the cumulative difference between y_true and y_score, both ordered according to y_scores array.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.expected_calibration_error
entries.summary: The Expected Calibration Error (ECE), which measures the difference between confidence scores and accuracy per bin.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.kolmogorov_smirnov_cdf
entries.summary: Compute the Kolmogorov-smirnov cumulative distribution function (CDF) for the float x. This is interpreted as the CDF of the maximum absolute value of the standard Brownian motion over the unit interval [0, 1]. The function is approximated by its power series, truncated so as to hit machine precision error.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.kolmogorov_smirnov_p_value
entries.summary: Compute Kolmogorov Smirnov p-value. Deduced from the corresponding statistic and CDF. It represents the probability of the observed statistic under the null hypothesis of perfect calibration.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.kolmogorov_smirnov_statistic
entries.summary: Compute Kolmogorov-smirnov's statistic for calibration test. Also called ECCE-MAD (Estimated Cumulative Calibration Errors - Maximum Absolute Deviation). The closer to zero, the better the scores are calibrated. Indeed, if the scores are perfectly calibrated, the cumulative differences between `y_true` and `y_score` should share the same properties of a standard Brownian motion asymptotically.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.kuiper_cdf
entries.summary: Compute the Kuiper cumulative distribution function (CDF) for the float x. This is interpreted as the CDF of the range of the standard Brownian motion over the unit interval [0, 1]. The function is approximated by its power series, truncated so as to hit machine precision error.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.kuiper_p_value
entries.summary: Compute Kuiper statistic p-value. Deduced from the corresponding statistic and CDF. It represents the probability of the observed statistic under the null hypothesis of perfect calibration.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.kuiper_statistic
entries.summary: Compute Kuiper's statistic for calibration test. Also called ECCE-R (Estimated Cumulative Calibration Errors - Range). The closer to zero, the better the scores are calibrated. Indeed, if the scores are perfectly calibrated, the cumulative differences between `y_true` and `y_score` should share the same properties of a standard Brownian motion asymptotically.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.length_scale
entries.summary: Compute the mean square root of the sum  of s * (1 - s). This is basically the standard deviation of the cumulative differences.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.sort_xy_by_y
entries.summary: Sort two arrays x and y according to y values.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.spiegelhalter_p_value
entries.summary: Compute Spiegelhalter statistic p-value. Deduced from the corresponding statistic and CDF, which is no more than the normal distribution. It represents the probability of the observed statistic under the null hypothesis of perfect calibration.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.spiegelhalter_statistic
entries.summary: Compute Spiegelhalter's statistic for calibration test. The closer to zero, the better the scores are calibrated. Indeed, if the scores are perfectly calibrated, the Brier score simplifies to an expression whose expectancy and variance are easy to compute. The statistic is no more that a z-score on this normalized expression.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.calibration.top_label_ece
entries.summary: The Top-Label ECE which is a method adapted to fit the ECE to a Top-Label setting [2].

entries.name: mapie.metrics.classification.classification_coverage_score
entries.summary: Effective coverage score obtained by the prediction sets.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.classification.classification_mean_width_score
entries.summary: Mean width of prediction set output by `mapie.classification._MapieClassifier`.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.classification.classification_ssc
entries.summary: Compute Size-Stratified Coverage metrics proposed in [3] that is the conditional coverage conditioned by the size of the predictions sets. The sets are ranked by their size (ascending) and then divided into num_bins groups: one value of coverage by groups is computed.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.classification.classification_ssc_score
entries.summary: Aggregate by the minimum for each confidence level the Size-Stratified Coverage [3]: returns the maximum violation of the conditional coverage (with the groups defined).

entries.name: mapie.metrics.conditional.coverage_gap
entries.summary: Compute the coverage gap across groups.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.conditional.excess_risk_target_coverage
entries.summary: Compute the excess risk of the target coverage.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.conditional.worst_slab_coverage
entries.summary: Compute the worst-case slab coverage.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.regression.coverage_width_based
entries.summary: Coverage Width-based Criterion (CWC) obtained by the prediction intervals.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.regression.hsic
entries.summary: Compute the square root of the hsic coefficient. HSIC is Hilbert-Schmidt independence criterion that is a correlation measure. Here we use it as proposed in [4], to compute the correlation between the indicator of coverage and the interval size.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.regression.regression_coverage_score
entries.summary: Effective coverage obtained by the prediction intervals.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.regression.regression_mean_width_score
entries.summary: Effective mean width score obtained by the prediction intervals.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.regression.regression_mwi_score
entries.summary: The Winkler score, proposed by Winkler (1972), is a measure used to evaluate prediction intervals, combining the length of the interval with a penalty that increases proportionally to the distance of an observation outside the interval.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.regression.regression_ssc
entries.summary: Compute Size-Stratified Coverage metrics proposed in [3] that is the conditional coverage conditioned by the size of the intervals. The intervals are ranked by their size (ascending) and then divided into num_bins groups: one value of coverage by groups is computed.

entries.name: mapie.metrics.regression.regression_ssc_score
entries.summary: Aggregate by the minimum for each confidence level the Size-Stratified Coverage [3]: returns the maximum violation of the conditional coverage (with the groups defined).

entries.name: mapie.metrics.uncertainty.auarc
entries.summary: Area Under the Accuracy-Rejection Curve (AUARC).

entries.name: mapie.risk_control.control_fwer
entries.summary: Apply a Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER) control procedure.

entries.name: mapie.risk_control.methods.compute_hoeffding_bentkus_p_value
entries.summary: The method computes the p_values according to the Hoeffding_Bentkus inequality for each alpha. We return the minimum between the Hoeffding and Bentkus p-values (Note that it depends on scipy.stats). The p_value is introduced in learn then test paper [1].

entries.name: mapie.risk_control.methods.find_best_predict_param
entries.summary: Find the higher value of lambda such that for all smaller lambda, the risk is smaller, for each value of alpha.

entries.name: mapie.risk_control.methods.find_precision_best_predict_param
entries.summary: Return the lambda that give the minimum precision along the lambdas that satisfy FWER control. Note: When a list in valid_index is empty, we can assume that lambda is equal to 1, as no lambda can verify the FWER control. And so to make our statement clear we also assume that the risk is high.

entries.name: mapie.risk_control.methods.get_r_hat_plus
entries.summary: Compute the upper bound of the loss for each lambda. The procedure here are the RCPS[1] and CRC [2] methods.

entries.name: mapie.risk_control.multi_label_classification.ltt_procedure
entries.summary: Apply the Learn-Then-Test procedure for risk control. Note that we will do a multiple test for `r_hat` that are less than level `alpha_np`. The procedure follows the instructions in [1]: - Calculate p-values for each lambdas discretized - Apply a family wise error rate algorithm, here Bonferonni correction - Return the index lambdas that give you the control at alpha level
